entries.symptom: No bundle URL present. Make sure you're running a packager server or have included a .jsbundle file in your application bundle.
entries.cause: A Debug build of the iOS app started while Metro was not running (or Metro runs on another port than the build expects); a Release build has the bundle embedded and never shows it
entries.fix: Start Metro for this project (npx expo start, or the port the dev client was built for) and reload the app; never switch the build to Release to hide it. For a release check, build the Release configuration on purpose

entries.symptom: Could not connect to development server (the red box when the app cannot fetch its bundle)
entries.cause: Metro is not running, or the device cannot reach it: on the Android emulator localhost is the emulator itself, and a physical device on another network cannot reach the computer
entries.fix: Start Metro; on the Android emulator forward the port to that one device (adb -s <serial> reverse tcp:8081 tcp:8081) or use 10.0.2.2; put a physical device on the same network. Never adb kill-server (it drops every session's devices); the Android "Unable to load script" red box is e2e-android-adb-reverse
match: Could not connect to development server

entries.symptom: Port 8081 is being used by another process (npx expo start asks to use another port)
entries.cause: Another Metro, often another project's or another session's, already listens on the port
entries.fix: Leave the other process alone (it may be another session's); start this project on its own port (npx expo start --port 8082) and point the dev client at it, or stop only a Metro you started
match: Port \d+ is being used by another process
Port \d+ is running this app in another window

entries.symptom: Error: EMFILE: too many open files, watch (Metro stops while starting or after a few reloads)
entries.cause: Metro's file watcher hit the macOS open-file limit; without Watchman it opens one handle per watched file
entries.fix: Install Watchman (Metro uses it when it is on the PATH) or raise the limit for that shell (ulimit -n 65536); keep watchFolders narrow. Never delete node_modules to make it go away

entries.symptom: Unable to resolve module <path> from <file>: None of these files exist
entries.cause: The import path is wrong (a typo, or a case difference that macOS tolerates and Linux CI does not), the package is not installed, or the @/ alias is not declared in tsconfig.json paths
entries.fix: Fix the import to the exact file name and case, install a missing package with npx expo install, and use the @/ alias the canonical tsconfig declares; tsc --noEmit finds the same import first

entries.symptom: Text strings must be rendered within a <Text> component.
entries.cause: A raw string or number is a child of a View: usually {count && <Badge />} with count 0 or an empty string, a stray character or space between JSX tags, or a translated string placed directly in a View
entries.fix: Wrap text in <Text> (the design-system Text component); write conditions as count > 0 ? <Badge /> : null so a falsy number is never rendered
match: Text strings must be rendered within a <Text> component

entries.symptom: VirtualizedLists should never be nested inside plain ScrollViews with the same orientation because it can break windowing and other functionality
entries.cause: A FlatList, SectionList or FlashList sits inside a ScrollView that scrolls the same way, so the list renders every row and loses recycling
entries.fix: Make the list the only scroller: move the content above and below into ListHeaderComponent and ListFooterComponent, or use one SectionList; never silence the warning with LogBox

entries.symptom: Invalid hook call. Hooks can only be called inside of the body of a function component
entries.cause: A hook is called outside a component or custom hook (an event handler, a plain helper, a class), or the bundle holds two copies of React (a package that brings its own react, or two versions in a workspace)
entries.fix: Call hooks only at the top level of components and use* hooks (react-hooks/rules-of-hooks catches it); npm ls react must show one version, otherwise dedupe or pin it

entries.symptom: Rendered more hooks than during the previous render, or Rendered fewer hooks than expected
entries.cause: A hook runs after an early return or inside a condition or loop, so the number of hooks differs between renders
entries.fix: Move every hook above the first early return and out of conditions; let react-hooks/rules-of-hooks run as an error

entries.symptom: Element type is invalid: expected a string (for built-in components) or a class/function (for composite components) but got: undefined
entries.cause: An import resolves to undefined: a default import of a named export (or the reverse), a circular import that is still undefined at render, or a component the installed library version no longer exports
entries.fix: Open the file named in "Check the render method of <Component>" and fix the import to the module's real export (house style: named exports); break the cycle by moving the shared piece into its own module

entries.symptom: Each child in a list should have a unique "key" prop.
entries.cause: A .map() returns elements without a key, or the keys repeat; a FlatList has no keyExtractor and its items have no key or id
entries.fix: Key each element by a stable id from the data (never the index for a list that reorders); give FlatList and FlashList a keyExtractor
match: Each child in a list should have a unique

entries.symptom: TypeError: Cannot read property '<name>' of undefined (Hermes), or undefined is not an object (evaluating '<expr>')
entries.cause: Code reads a field of a value that is undefined at run time: data used before it loaded, a field missing from stored or server data, or an import that resolved to undefined
entries.fix: Read the first frame in your own code in the stack; validate data where it enters (the schema at the boundary) and model the loading state in the type instead of asserting it; keep noUncheckedIndexedAccess on

entries.symptom: ReferenceError: Property 'crypto' doesn't exist (a uuid or id library calls crypto.getRandomValues or crypto.randomUUID)
entries.cause: Hermes has no Web Crypto global, so code written for browsers or Node finds no crypto object
entries.fix: Generate ids and random bytes through expo-crypto (randomUUID, getRandomValues) behind your own port; for a library that needs the global, load a crypto polyfill at the entry before that library is imported

entries.symptom: requireNativeComponent: '<Name>' was not found in the UIManager, or The package '<name>' doesn't seem to be linked
entries.cause: JavaScript and the installed native binary disagree: a package with native code was added or upgraded after the dev build was made, or the app runs in Expo Go, which holds only Expo's own modules
entries.fix: Rebuild the development build after any native dependency change (npx expo run:ios or run:android, or a new development build) and install versions with npx expo install; reloading JavaScript cannot add native code
match: requireNativeComponent: .{1,60} was not found in the UIManager

entries.symptom: Attempted to navigate before mounting the Root Layout component. Ensure the Root Layout component is rendering a Slot, or other navigator on the first render.
entries.cause: The root layout returns null or a loading view instead of its navigator while it loads, or an effect calls router.replace before the navigator has mounted
entries.fix: Always render the navigator from the root layout and keep the splash screen up while loading; send the user with <Redirect> in a screen or with Stack.Protected guards, never with router calls in the root layout's first effects
match: navigate before mounting the Root Layout

entries.symptom: The action 'NAVIGATE' with payload {"name":"<route>"} was not handled by any navigator, or No route named "<route>" exists in nested children
entries.cause: The href does not match a route file: a typo, a route group or folder left out of the path, a file outside the app folder, or a screen of a navigator that is not mounted
entries.fix: Navigate by the route's real path and turn on typed routes so tsc checks every href; list the screen in its layout when the layout names its screens
match: was not handled by any navigator
No route named .{1,80} exists in nested children

entries.symptom: Couldn't find a navigation context. Have you wrapped your app with 'NavigationContainer'?
entries.cause: A navigation hook runs outside the router tree (a component rendered above the root navigator or in a test render without the router), or a second copy of @react-navigation/native is installed
entries.fix: Use expo-router's hooks inside routes, test screens with expo-router's renderRouter, and keep one @react-navigation/native version (npm ls @react-navigation/native)

entries.symptom: TypeError: Network request failed
entries.cause: The request never reached a server: Android blocks plain http:// by default, iOS App Transport Security blocks it too, localhost on the Android emulator is the emulator itself, the TLS certificate is self-signed, or the device is offline
entries.fix: Use https everywhere; reach a local server through the variant's API URL (adb -s <serial> reverse, or the computer's address) and allow cleartext only in the development variant through a config plugin; let the ApiClient map this error to its typed network failure so the screen shows the offline state

entries.symptom: Data stays stale after the app returns to the foreground or the network comes back, although refetchOnWindowFocus and refetchOnReconnect are on
entries.cause: React Native has no window focus or online events, so TanStack Query never learns that the app became active or that the network returned
entries.fix: Wire focusManager to AppState and onlineManager to the connectivity port once at startup (the networking skill's template)

entries.symptom: A query refetches on every render or its cache never hits; two screens show different data for the same item
entries.cause: The query key holds a new object or function each render, or leaves out a value the queryFn reads, so the cache entry changes or is shared wrongly
entries.fix: Build keys from a key factory of plain values only, and put every variable the queryFn uses into its key

entries.symptom: An update was published but the installed app keeps running the bundle it was built with
entries.cause: The update went to a branch the build's channel does not point to, its runtime version differs from the build's (a native change moved the fingerprint), or it downloaded in the background and applies only at the next cold start
entries.fix: Compare the build's channel and runtime version with the update's; republish to the right branch or ship a new store build when the runtime changed; kill and relaunch the app to load a downloaded update

entries.symptom: Crash reports show minified frames (index.android.bundle or main.jsbundle line 1 with a large column) instead of source files
entries.cause: The source maps and debug IDs of that build or update were never uploaded: the auth token was missing from the build environment, Metro does not use the crash reporter's serializer, or an over-the-air update was published without its own upload
entries.fix: Give the build environment the upload token as a secret, use the crash reporter's Metro config so bundles carry debug IDs, and upload source maps for every update you publish; confirm the release shows its artifacts before the next crash

entries.symptom: After deleting and reinstalling the app on iOS, the user is still signed in or an old token is sent
entries.cause: iOS keeps keychain items when an app is deleted, so expo-secure-store values outlive the install while app storage starts empty
entries.fix: On first launch, when app storage holds no install marker, delete the secure-store keys and then write the marker

entries.symptom: An https link to your domain opens Safari instead of the app
entries.cause: iOS could not verify the domain: apple-app-site-association is not served at /.well-known/ over https without redirects, its appID (team ID plus bundle id) does not match the build, or associatedDomains lacks applinks:<domain>
entries.fix: Serve the association file unredirected with the matching appID and path rules, add applinks:<domain> to the variant's associated domains, then reinstall the app (iOS fetches the file at install)

entries.symptom: An https link to your domain shows a chooser or opens the browser instead of the app on Android
entries.cause: Android did not verify the App Link: assetlinks.json is not served at /.well-known/, or its SHA-256 fingerprints lack the key that signs the installed build (the Play app-signing key for store installs)
entries.fix: List every signing key's SHA-256 in assetlinks.json, keep autoVerify on the intent filter, reinstall, and read the state with adb -s <serial> shell pm get-app-links <package>
